page.overview:
What is Barad-dûr?

Barad-dûr ("Dark Fortress") was Sauron's central stronghold in Mordor, serving as his seat of power in Middle-earth in the Second Age until its end and again in the late Third Age after its rebuilding. Its final destruction happened a few years before the end of the Third Age.

Barad-dûr was sustained by dark magic and was the greatest fortress in Middle-earth of its time. It was built in the Second Age, and leveled after Sauron's defeat in the War of the Last Alliance. Sauron rebuilt it late in the Third Age as he regained his power, but it was forever destroyed immediately upon the destruction of the One Ring.

In his writings, J.R.R. Tolkien describes little of the tower besides its terror, color, and surreal size.

Following Sauron's occupation of the land of Mordor in SA 1000, he began making plans for the construction of a vast and powerful fortress, to serve as his seat of power.
